chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl, altogether from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about Tayammum, so he struck the ground with his hand, then raised it and shook it, then wiped with it his two foreheads and his two palms once.
ai.seo_question: How is Tayammum performed according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah, provides a concise procedural account of Tayammum as practiced by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing the simplicity of the act involving a single strike and wipe. It serves as a foundational text for the Shia jurisprudence of dry ablution, confirming the validity of using earth/dust when water is unavailable or its use is harmful. The description highlights the physical mechanics of purification, reinforcing the ritual's role as a valid substitute for Wudu in specific conditions.
